must_identify.item: The failing requests come from the pod of a separate Deployment shop-api, which shares the app=api label and is therefore an endpoint of the api Service
must_identify.evidence: Deployment shop-api (namespace shop, image python:3.12-alpine, created 2026-10-16T08:37:30Z) sets its pod template label to app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api — i.e. it accidentally shares app=api with the real api deployment.

must_identify.item: That pod returns 500 because its config lacks DATABASE_URL (KeyError), while the real api pods are healthy
must_identify.evidence: The shop-api container's app.py requires DATABASE_URL, which isn't set in its deployment env (only REDIS_HOST=redis is defined). Every /items request throws: KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' ... Confirmed clean: the two real api pods (api-f64486c4c-m9rfh, api-f64486c4c-pf4tk) log only 200 for /items//healthz

notes: The primary fix is relabeling the shop-api pods so the api Service no longer selects them, with scale-to-0 or delete as a follow-up option. Both are acceptable. The 'what changed' section describes a namespace-wide redeploy and frames it as speculation. It does not contradict the injected change.
